A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same frozen CLIP-ViT forgery-detection research, renamed from GFF to ForgeLens. Their readable methods, equations, results, figures and complete appendices support comparison despite substantial revision.

before.justification: V1 reports original detection results, component ablations, robustness experiments and feature visualizations in the main text and appendix.

after.justification: V2 reports original UniversalFakeDetect and GenImage results, training-data-size experiments, ablations, robustness tests and feature analyses.

M1.justification: V2 introduces weight sharing across groups of ViT blocks through WSGM, replacing v1's separate per-block DFGMs. The bottleneck transformation, frozen encoder, multi-stage CLS-token fusion and two-stage training remain. FAFormer largely renames FuseFormer, making cross-block parameter sharing a localized architectural revision.

E1.justification: V2's UniversalFakeDetect comparison adds SITD, SAN, CRN and IMLE coverage. StyleGAN2, PNDM and VQ-Diffusion disappear from the main quantitative comparison, although some remain in visualizations or other evaluation coverage. Appendix C.2 adds GenImage, including SDv1.4 training and evaluation on Stable Diffusion, Midjourney, Wukong and other generators.

E2.justification: V2 adds Patchfor, F3Net and C2P-CLIP to main comparisons, Adapter and LoRA in Table 4, and additional architectures and detectors in GenImage Table 10. BiHPF and FrePGAN disappear from result tables; robustness comparisons drop UniFD and FatFormer. V1's Wang baseline is retained under the name CNN-Spot.

E3.justification: V1's 1-, 2- and 4-class training comparisons become a four-class training-size sweep from 1% to 100%. The reported UniversalFakeDetect configuration changes stage epochs from 3/1 to 50/10, batch sizes from 32/128 to 16/16, and the second-stage learning rate from 5e-6 to 2e-6. V2 also introduces 400-image GenImage training and combined perturbations applied to training and test data.

E4.justification: V2 adds training-size sensitivity, Adapter/LoRA comparisons, WSGM-count ablations and combined-corruption testing, while revising bottleneck and fusion-depth sweeps. Figure 2 expands feature analysis with ResNet50 and explicit seen/unseen comparisons. The parameter-count comparison in v1 Table A3 is removed. Most appendix CAM images are retained rather than new analyses.

E5.justification: Neither version clearly reports seeds, confidence intervals or error bars. However, v2 Table 10 newly states that accuracy is averaged over eight training cases while also specifying training only on SDv1.4. Those cases are undefined, leaving uncertainty about whether repeated-run averaging or aggregation across training domains was introduced.

E6.justification: V1 reports four-class GAN and diffusion mean ACC/AP of 98.7/99.9 and 97.5/99.8. V2 replaces these summaries with 94.99/98.83 over its different UniversalFakeDetect configuration and adds 97.6% GenImage accuracy, training-size results and revised ablation/robustness entries. These are changed or newly reported results, not directly comparable performance gains between versions.

T1.justification: Section 3.2 of v2 adds a formal sharing constraint: m guidance modules cover n ViT blocks in groups of n/m, requiring an integer group size, with indexed WSGM modules in Equation 1. The remaining transformer and fusion formulations are substantially retained; no theorems or proofs are added.

C1.justification: V1 emphasizes efficient guidance/fusion, optimal performance within five epochs and high GAN/diffusion accuracy. V2 makes data efficiency a central contribution, claiming state-of-the-art detection with only 1% of training data and emphasizing weight sharing. Generalizable forgery-specific feature extraction remains the shared central premise.

C2.justification: V2 adds an explanation linking blur/noise failures to weakened forgery artifacts and identifies two-stage training complexity and FAFormer tuning as limitations. V1's single-class overfitting discussion and limited-diversity explanation of hyperparameter sensitivity are dropped. The broader interpretation that guidance suppresses forgery-irrelevant features remains.

D1.justification: V2 adds dataset sizes and class balances, sampling information, perturbation-strength ranges, learning-rate schedules, module counts and attention-head settings in Appendices A, B and D. It also supplies a code-repository link absent from v1. Some GenImage settings remain ranges rather than exact configurations, and v1's explicit parameter-count disclosure is removed.

R1.justification: V2 expands positioning around data efficiency and distinguishes specialized, preprocessing-based and frozen-model approaches. It adds substantive discussion or comparison involving C2P-CLIP, AdaptFormer/Adapter and LoRA, together with GenImage and additional detection literature. This extends the comparison beyond v1's principal focus on existing forgery detectors and frozen CLIP features.

P1.justification: The title, method terminology, abstract, introduction, related work and conclusions are extensively rewritten. V2 separates experimental setup from results, introduces numbered sections and organized appendices, and moves references before the appendix. These are substantial narrative and structural revisions beyond added experiments.

P2.justification: V2 redraws the conceptual and architecture diagrams, expands the t-SNE figure, adds a training-size chart, and reorganizes main results into separate accuracy and AP tables across a combined benchmark. Dataset and hyperparameter tables are added. CAM panels are rearranged and relabeled, largely reusing v1 images.

improvement.justification: The training-size sweep, diffusion-trained GenImage evaluation and detailed dataset, perturbation and training specifications strengthen empirical support and reproducibility. These gains are offset partly by removing explicit parameter-count and comparative robustness evidence. V2 also contains reporting inconsistencies, including Table 10's conflicting training/averaging description and a stated FatFormer gain that disagrees with Table 1. Overall, the evidence supports a limited net improvement.
